Kruti Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kruti, Ukraine

Not demolished. This cemetery's founding is undocumented, though its earliest gravestone dates to 1752; no postwar burials exist, confirming the Jewish community was never reestablished after the Holocaust. Epigraphic data collected by the ESJF in 2018 traces the community itself to 1750; population reached 2,068 by 1849 and 2,389 (50% of residents) by 1897. A Talmud Torah operated from 1910, with five synagogues by 1914; Jewish-owned businesses included chemists, pharmacy warehouses, forest warehouses, a hotel, a mill, and 54 market stalls. Population reached about 1,800 (90% of residents) by 1930. Kruti's Jewish community was entirely exterminated during the Shoah.
